formation.explanation: Append is buffered during prepare, sent locally during Leader/Accept, or forwarded. Current-ballot promises populate participant slots; a prepare quorum selects maximal accepted-round/index history, synchronizes it, then sends AcceptSync. Followers synchronize and acknowledge, and incremental appends use sequence validation. Current-ballot Accepted messages update leader indexes; a write quorum causes decided-index advancement and decision propagation. Read APIs expose the decided prefix for application use. Storage load reconstructs accepted extent and reads classify entries against the decided boundary. The optional actor tracks a client EntryId to an assigned end index and ballot; on ticks it resolves success using decided index before testing ballot supersession.

context.explanation: Tick drives BLE; matching heartbeat rounds/configurations influence leader selection. SequencePaxos requires a higher ballot before initiating preparation. Followers persist a higher promise, reject lower-ballot replication and accept same-ballot prepare only during recovery. Reconnect and sequence gaps can initiate equal-ballot recovery. StopSign seals the old log and delegates startup/state transfer of a new configuration to the caller. Construction reads the stored promise into protocol and BLE recovery context, while cached accepted metadata comes from the backend. The actor serializes incoming messages and commands but runs completion processing only on tick branches.

connection.explanation: Authority alone does not enable acceptance: the new leader first gathers promise support and adopts accepted history, including prior decisions, before appending buffered work. A stopped selected history blocks appends. Followers require the promised ballot and appropriate phase; incremental old-session work is rejected or triggers recovery. Equal-ballot recovery resets phase and sequence before synchronization, leaving a specific delayed-AcceptSync history question. Client assignment records survive incoming higher-ballot synchronization until a later notifier drain. Whether the assigned entry survives depends on adopted history, rather than on numeric decided-index advancement alone.
